fixed_decision_rule.mandatory: All mapped backend oracles, common supervision/authority, upstream source/image-qualified E2E and native-receipt parity pass three repetitions. Source/synthetic review alone cannot qualify. Score deletion protection independently; its failure cannot retire telemetry.
fixed_decision_rule.rank: If only one backend qualifies select it. If both qualify choose an arm with >=10% lower median elapsed, provided RSS is not >10% higher. Otherwise, if neither has material elapsed advantage, choose an arm with >=10% lower median RSS, provided elapsed is not >10% higher. Opposing material tradeoffs retain both as co-qualified, no automatic winner.
fixed_decision_rule.tie: Within both tolerances retain both measured source/image-bound arms as co-qualified, with equality and no superiority/automatic installed-path selection.
fixed_decision_rule.none_qualify: Retire only unsupported backend role with failures, not separately qualified supervision/isolation/recovery.
fixed_decision_rule.terminal: FINAL also requires verdict/wave/next_review and actual selected deployed runs[] source/image binding, upstream E2E and invoke or role reason at the adopted pin. Co-qualification alone is not FINAL.
fixed_decision_rule.failure_retention: Retain every failed install/deployment, restart, alert, attack, restore and missing sample; no silent retry/dropped repetition.
fixed_decision_rule.amendments: Input corrections require independent reviewed hashed amendments before scoring; never change arms/gates/metrics/tolerances after replay.
fixed_decision_rule.total_outcome: Evaluate elapsed advantage with 10*x<=9*y and the RSS guard 10*x_rss<=11*y_rss in both directions. If exactly one direction qualifies select it. If neither elapsed direction qualifies and neither has any elapsed material advantage, apply the same RSS advantage and elapsed guard. If no single arm is selected, retain both as co-qualified with the measured tolerance/tradeoff classification. All conditions use exact integers.

recovery_subrole.basis: The 09-26 survivor challenges compromised-client deletion and off-host recovery independently of telemetry selection.

arms.path_rule: Explicit persistent owned path on an independent host, sealed separately per repetition; never the temporary default.
arms.source_version_reason: The proposal reviewed v0.14.0; this locked current source tests append-only/private-repository/TLS behavior through its own build/tests. No old receipt transfers.

arms.expectation: Writable SFTP control permits forget/prune and direct data deletion; success is expected threat-model control behavior, not protection acceptance.

arms.path_rule: Explicit persistent isolated destination, TLS and per-fixture authentication; same destination resources and data seal.

immutable_snapshot_disposition.reason: No independently administered immutable-snapshot filesystem/source pin/destination policy is selected in retained inputs. A generic filesystem feature is not an executable protection arm. The required destination-capability receipt must establish this absence before this three-arm configuration can run.
immutable_snapshot_disposition.reopen_rule: If the actual destination already has immutable snapshots with the same protection, halt before scoring and add the retained mechanism through a reviewed hashed amendment. Do not score around it or claim rest-server adds value.

oracle.attack_boundary: Research-client backup identity has no destination admin/snapshot rights. All attacks use disposable seeded stores on an independent owned destination.
oracle.protected_expected: Both client attacks are refused; seeded source hashes/snapshots stay intact; check --read-data and fresh-target restore --verify exit 0 with byte-identical fixture state.
oracle.sftp_expected: Both attacks succeed on disposable writable SFTP. Use separately seeded attack and restore stores; destructive control success is not restoration qualification.
oracle.private_repository_isolation: Two fictional principals cannot read/write/delete each other repository; TLS identity is verified with no plaintext fallback.
oracle.destination_identity: Retain independent-host and persistent-path proof privately; publish scoped redacted attestation and fictional hashes only.
oracle.live_state: Quiesce owned fixture, flush/checkpoint fictional SQLite, seal public hash manifest, back up, close source, restore into empty independent target, restart restored services and query the same oracle.

fixed_decision_rule.mandatory: Protected arms pass all deletion-refusal/isolation/TLS/off-host/fresh-restore oracles in three repetitions. SFTP must reproduce the expected destructive control.
fixed_decision_rule.rank: This sub-role decides deletion protection, not speed. SFTP must reproduce its expected writable-control behavior. Co-qualify every protected mechanism that passes all required protection/restore fields; report any differences without a superiority ranking.
fixed_decision_rule.tie: If both protected mechanisms pass, retain both as co-qualified for this protection scope; no unmeasured default is adopted.
fixed_decision_rule.none_qualify: Retire only unsupported deletion protection with failures, never telemetry/dashboards/alerting by this protection failure.

measurement_protocol.clock: monotonic_ns on one measurement host per pair; retain all raw timestamps
measurement_protocol.elapsed_start: Immediately before first native ingest action in usage-parity after clean owned deployments report ready; install/startup excluded and separately retained.
measurement_protocol.elapsed_stop: Immediately after final native response validating failure-alert-delivery, including all scored restarts/restores/UI queries in declared order.
measurement_protocol.recovery_elapsed_start: Immediately before check --read-data on seeded destination after attack verification.
measurement_protocol.recovery_elapsed_stop: Immediately after fresh-target restored-service query validation, including restore --verify and restored startup.
measurement_protocol.rss_process_set: All isolated arm-cgroup descendants/containers, including backend stores, Collector, UI/alert services, arm-specific notifications and transient backup/restore children. Exclude identical external driver/browser/recorder and separately scored common sandbox/supervisor; report their costs separately.
measurement_protocol.rss_aggregation: Every 50ms sum concurrent /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS bytes for all live descendants; take maximum sum in interval, not sum of independent per-process maxima. Retain all samples/PID membership.
measurement_protocol.missing_sample_rule: Missing membership/permissions/sample disqualifies repetition; no zero substitution.
measurement_protocol.summaries: Median of three complete elapsed_ns values and median of three simultaneous RSS peaks; exact retained integers, not rounded displays.
measurement_protocol.material_advantage: X materially beats Y iff X <= 0.90 * Y, using exact integer ratios; boundary equality counts. No post-run threshold choice.
diagnostic_only: full correctness is eligibility, not rank
provider cost and native usage are identical source-task replay diagnostics
measurement_protocol.pre_run_seal: Exact native commands, queries/panel definitions/alert routes, polling, cgroup membership and images sealed before replay; input changes require reviewed hashed amendments before scoring.
measurement_protocol.common_gate_phase: Authority and process-supervision gates execute before scored ingest; independently scored deletion protection executes outside backend timing/RSS intervals.
